hc.name: Mike LaFleur
hc.bio: Mike LaFleur is the head coach of the Arizona Cardinals in 2026, hired February 1, 2026 as the franchise's 45th head coach after three seasons (2023–2025) as Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator. He played quarterback and safety at Elmhurst (2005–2008), then coached in college at Elmhurst, Saint Joseph's (IN), and Davidson before NFL stops as an intern with the Cleveland Browns (2014), offensive assistant with the Atlanta Falcons (2015–2016), passing-game coordinator with the San Francisco 49ers (2017–2020), and Jets offensive coordinator (2021–2022). He is the younger brother of Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur.

oc.name: Nathaniel Hackett
oc.bio: Nathaniel Hackett is the Arizona Cardinals' offensive coordinator in 2026. He previously was offensive coordinator for Buffalo, Jacksonville, Green Bay (2019–2021), and the New York Jets (2023–2024), and was Denver Broncos head coach in 2022 before being fired during that season. In 2025 he was a defensive analyst for the Green Bay Packers under Matt LaFleur.

dc.name: Nick Rallis
dc.bio: Nick Rallis is the Arizona Cardinals' defensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2023 (first under Jonathan Gannon, then Mike LaFleur). He played college football at Minnesota and previously was a Vikings defensive quality-control coach (2018–2020) and Eagles linebackers coach (2021–2022).

st.name: Michael Ghobrial
st.bio: Michael Ghobrial is the Arizona Cardinals' special teams coordinator in 2026. He played college football at UCLA and was New York Giants special teams coordinator in 2024–2025 after assistant special teams work with the Jets (2021–2023) and a 2017 Lions fellowship.

hc.name: Kevin Stefanski
hc.bio: Kevin Stefanski is the Atlanta Falcons' head coach in 2026, hired January 17, 2026 on a five-year contract after Cleveland fired him in January 2026. He played safety at Penn (2000–2004), spent 2006–2019 with the Minnesota Vikings (offensive coordinator in 2018–2019), and was Browns head coach from 2020 to 2025, going 45–56 in the regular season and winning AP NFL Coach of the Year in 2020 and 2023.

oc.name: Tommy Rees
oc.bio: Tommy Rees is the Atlanta Falcons' offensive coordinator and play-caller in 2026 under Kevin Stefanski. A former Notre Dame quarterback (2010–2013), he was a Chargers offensive assistant in 2016, then Browns pass-game specialist/tight ends coach in 2024 and Browns offensive coordinator in 2025 (play-caller from Week 10).

dc.name: Jeff Ulbrich
dc.bio: Jeff Ulbrich is the Atlanta Falcons' defensive coordinator in 2026, retained after serving as DC in 2025. He played linebacker at Hawaii and for the San Francisco 49ers (2000–2009), was Jets defensive coordinator (2021–2024) and interim Jets head coach from October 8, 2024, and earlier coached linebackers in Atlanta (2015–2020).

st.name: Craig Aukerman
st.bio: Craig Aukerman is the Atlanta Falcons' special teams coordinator in 2026. He previously held the same title for the San Diego Chargers (2016), Tennessee Titans (2018–2023), and Miami Dolphins (2025), with earlier NFL assistant special teams stops in Jacksonville and Tennessee.

hc.name: Dave Canales
hc.bio: Dave Canales is the Carolina Panthers' head coach in 2026, in his third season after signing a six-year deal on January 25, 2024. He played wide receiver at Azusa Pacific (1999–2003), spent 2010–2022 as a Seahawks offensive assistant under Pete Carroll (Super Bowl XLVIII), was Tampa Bay offensive coordinator in 2023, and led Carolina to an 8–9 NFC South title and a wild-card loss in 2025 (career regular-season record 13–21).

oc.name: Brad Idzik
oc.bio: Brad Idzik is the Carolina Panthers' offensive coordinator in 2026 and the designated play-caller. He was a Seahawks assistant (2019–2022) and Buccaneers wide receivers coach in 2023 before becoming Panthers OC in 2024.

dc.name: Ejiro Evero
dc.bio: Ejiro Evero is the Carolina Panthers' defensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2023 (Frank Reich, then Dave Canales). Born January 6, 1981, he has NFL assistant stops with Tampa Bay, San Francisco, Green Bay, the Rams (safeties 2017–2020; secondary/passing-game coordinator 2021), and was Denver Broncos defensive coordinator in 2022.

st.name: Tracy Smith
st.bio: Tracy Smith is the Carolina Panthers' special teams coordinator in 2026, a title he has held since 2024. His NFL path includes assistant special teams jobs with Cleveland, San Francisco, Oakland, Houston, and Seattle, plus Texans special teams coordinator in 2020.

hc.name: Ben Johnson
hc.bio: Ben Johnson is the Chicago Bears' head coach in 2026, hired January 21, 2025 after three seasons as Detroit Lions offensive coordinator (2022–2024). He was a walk-on quarterback at North Carolina (2004–2007) and, in his first Bears season, went 11–6, won the NFC North, and beat Green Bay in the wild-card round before an overtime loss to the Rams (regular-season record 11–6).

oc.name: Press Taylor
oc.bio: Press Taylor is the Chicago Bears' offensive coordinator in 2026 after serving as passing-game coordinator in 2025. He was an Eagles assistant from 2013 to 2020, Colts senior offensive assistant in 2021, and Jacksonville Jaguars offensive coordinator from 2022 to 2024.

dc.name: Dennis Allen
dc.bio: Dennis Allen is the Chicago Bears' defensive coordinator in 2026, hired with Ben Johnson in 2025. A former safety, he was Oakland Raiders head coach (2012–2014) and New Orleans Saints head coach (2022–2024), and was Saints defensive coordinator from 2015 to 2021.

st.name: Richard Hightower
st.bio: Richard Hightower is the Chicago Bears' special teams coordinator in 2026, a role he has held with the club since 2022 (retained by Ben Johnson). He was San Francisco 49ers special teams coordinator from 2017 to 2021 after earlier NFL assistant special teams work in Houston, Washington, San Francisco, and Chicago.

hc.name: Brian Schottenheimer
hc.bio: Brian Schottenheimer is the Dallas Cowboys' head coach in 2026, promoted January 24, 2025 after serving as Cowboys offensive coordinator (2023–2024). A former Kansas and Florida quarterback (backup on Florida's 1996 national champions), he was Jets OC (2006–2011), Rams OC (2012–2014), Seahawks OC (2018–2020), and went 7–9–1 in his first Cowboys season (2025).

oc.name: Klayton Adams
oc.bio: Klayton Adams is the Dallas Cowboys' offensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2025. He was Colts assistant offensive line coach (2019–2020) and tight ends coach (2021–2022), then Arizona Cardinals offensive line coach (2023–2024).

dc.name: Christian Parker
dc.bio: Christian Parker is the Dallas Cowboys' defensive coordinator in 2026. He was a Packers defensive quality-control coach (2019–2020), Broncos defensive backs coach (2021–2023), and Eagles passing-game coordinator and defensive backs coach (2024–2025).

st.name: Nick Sorensen
st.bio: Nick Sorensen is the Dallas Cowboys' special teams coordinator in 2026, a title he has held since 2025. A former Virginia Tech safety who played 10 NFL seasons, he coached Seahawks special teams and secondary (2013–2020), was Jaguars ST coordinator in 2021, and was San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator in 2024.

hc.name: Dan Campbell
hc.bio: Dan Campbell is the Detroit Lions' head coach in 2026, in his sixth season after being hired January 20, 2021. A former Texas A&M tight end drafted by the Giants in 1999 (third round), he played 11 NFL seasons and was Miami interim head coach in 2015. With Detroit he is 48–36–1 in the regular season, including a 15–2 NFC No. 1 seed in 2024; the Lions were 9–8 and missed the playoffs in 2025.

oc.name: Drew Petzing
oc.bio: Drew Petzing is the Detroit Lions' offensive coordinator in 2026. He played at Middlebury (2005–2006) and was Arizona Cardinals offensive coordinator from 2023 to 2025 after Browns tight ends (2020–2021) and quarterbacks (2022) jobs and earlier Vikings assistant roles (2014–2019).

dc.name: Kelvin Sheppard
dc.bio: Kelvin Sheppard is the Detroit Lions' defensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2025. He played linebacker at LSU and eight NFL seasons (Bills third-round pick, 2011) and has coached Lions outside linebackers (2021) and linebackers (2022–2024) under Dan Campbell.

st.name: Dave Fipp
st.bio: Dave Fipp is the Detroit Lions' special teams coordinator in 2026, a title he has held since 2021. He was Philadelphia Eagles special teams coordinator from 2013 to 2020 after 49ers and Dolphins assistant special teams work (2008–2012).

hc.name: Matt LaFleur
hc.bio: Matt LaFleur is the Green Bay Packers' head coach in 2026, hired January 8, 2019 and given a multiyear extension January 17, 2026. He played quarterback at Saginaw Valley State after two years at Western Michigan, then was Rams OC (2017), Titans OC (2018), and Packers HC with a 76–40–1 regular-season record through 2025 (nine playoff games, 3–6). His younger brother Mike is Arizona's 2026 head coach.

oc.name: Adam Stenavich
oc.bio: Adam Stenavich is the Green Bay Packers' offensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2022. A former Michigan offensive tackle signed by Carolina as an undrafted free agent, he was 49ers assistant offensive line coach (2017–2018) and Packers offensive line coach (2019–2021, plus run-game coordinator in 2021).

dc.name: Jonathan Gannon
dc.bio: Jonathan Gannon is the Green Bay Packers' defensive coordinator in 2026 after three seasons as Arizona Cardinals head coach (2023–2025). He played at Louisville and was Eagles defensive coordinator (2021–2022), helping Philadelphia reach Super Bowl LVII, after Colts and Vikings defensive backs jobs.

st.name: Cam Achord
st.bio: Cam Achord is the Green Bay Packers' special teams coordinator in 2026, named February 27, 2026. He was Patriots assistant special teams coach (2018–2019) and special teams coordinator (2020–2023), then Giants assistant special teams coach in 2024–2025.

hc.name: Sean McVay
hc.bio: Sean McVay is the Los Angeles Rams' head coach in 2026, in his 10th season after being hired January 12, 2017 as the NFL's then-youngest modern-era head coach. He played wide receiver at Miami (OH) (2004–2008) and won Super Bowl LVI in the 2021 season; through 2025 he is 92–57 in the regular season and 10–6 in the playoffs, including an NFC Championship loss to Seattle after the 2025 season. The Rams announced a contract extension for McVay and GM Les Snead after that season.

oc.name: Nate Scheelhaase
oc.bio: Nate Scheelhaase is the Los Angeles Rams' offensive coordinator in 2026, promoted after Mike LaFleur left to become Cardinals head coach. He played quarterback at Illinois (2009–2013) and was a Rams offensive assistant/pass-game specialist in 2024 and pass-game coordinator in 2025.

dc.name: Chris Shula
dc.bio: Chris Shula is the Los Angeles Rams' defensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2024. A former Miami (OH) linebacker and grandson of Don Shula, he has been on Sean McVay's Rams staff since 2017 in linebacker and pass-game roles after Chargers quality-control work (2015–2016).

st.name: Bubba Ventrone
st.bio: Bubba Ventrone is the Los Angeles Rams' special teams coordinator in 2026. A former Villanova safety who played for the Patriots, Jets, Browns, and 49ers, he was Patriots assistant special teams coach (2015–2017), Colts ST coordinator (2018–2022), and Browns assistant head coach/ST coordinator (2023–2025).

hc.name: Kevin O'Connell
hc.bio: Kevin O'Connell is the Minnesota Vikings' head coach in 2026, hired February 16, 2022 after winning Super Bowl LVI as Rams offensive coordinator. A San Diego State quarterback drafted by New England in the third round in 2008, he played five NFL seasons and was AP NFL Coach of the Year in 2024 after a 14–3 regular season. Through 2025 his Vikings regular-season record is 43–25.

oc.name: Wes Phillips
oc.bio: Wes Phillips is the Minnesota Vikings' offensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2022 under Kevin O'Connell. A former quarterback and the son of Wade Phillips (grandson of Bum Phillips), he coached tight ends for Dallas, Washington, and the Rams before becoming Rams pass-game coordinator/tight ends coach in 2021.

dc.name: Brian Flores
dc.bio: Brian Flores is the Minnesota Vikings' defensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2023. He spent 2008–2018 with the Patriots (defensive play-caller in 2018; Super Bowl LIII) and was Miami Dolphins head coach from 2019 to 2021, then Steelers senior defensive assistant/linebackers coach in 2022.

st.name: Matt Daniels
st.bio: Matt Daniels is the Minnesota Vikings' special teams coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2022. He played safety at Duke and was signed by the St. Louis Rams as an undrafted free agent in 2012, then was Rams (2018–2019) and Cowboys (2020–2021) assistant special teams coach.

hc.name: Kellen Moore
hc.bio: Kellen Moore is the New Orleans Saints' head coach in 2026, hired February 11, 2025 after one season as Eagles offensive coordinator and Super Bowl LIX. He played quarterback at Boise State (FBS career wins record, 49–3 as a starter) and in the NFL with Detroit and Dallas (2012–2017), then was Cowboys OC (2019–2022) and Chargers OC (2023). His first Saints season ended 6–11.

oc.name: Doug Nussmeier
oc.bio: Doug Nussmeier is the New Orleans Saints' offensive coordinator in 2026, a title he has held since 2025. A former Idaho quarterback and 1994 Saints draft pick, his recent NFL coaching includes Cowboys tight ends (2018–2019) and quarterbacks (2020–2022), Chargers quarterbacks (2023), and Eagles quarterbacks (2024).

dc.name: Brandon Staley
dc.bio: Brandon Staley is the New Orleans Saints' defensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2025. He was Los Angeles Chargers head coach from 2021 to 2023 (fired December 15, 2023), Rams defensive coordinator in 2020, and 49ers assistant head coach/defense in 2024.

st.name: Phil Galiano
st.bio: Phil Galiano is the New Orleans Saints' special teams coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2025. He played at Shippensburg and was Saints assistant special teams coach from 2019 to 2024 after Buccaneers assistant ST (2012–2013) and a 2016 Dolphins internship.

hc.name: John Harbaugh
hc.bio: John Harbaugh is the New York Giants' head coach in 2026, hired January 20, 2026 on a five-year contract after Baltimore fired him January 6, 2026. He played safety at Miami (OH) (1980–1983), spent 1998–2007 with the Eagles, and was Ravens head coach from 2008 to 2025 (180–113 regular season, Super Bowl XLVII, AP Coach of the Year 2019).

oc.name: Matt Nagy
oc.bio: Matt Nagy is the New York Giants' offensive coordinator in 2026 under John Harbaugh. A former Delaware quarterback who later played in the Arena Football League, he was Chicago Bears head coach (2018–2021) and Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator in 2016–2017 and 2023–2025.

dc.name: Dennard Wilson
dc.bio: Dennard Wilson is the New York Giants' defensive coordinator in 2026. A former Maryland safety signed by Washington in 2004, he was Tennessee Titans defensive coordinator in 2024–2025 after defensive backs jobs with the Rams, Jets, Eagles, and Ravens.

st.name: Chris Horton
st.bio: Chris Horton is the New York Giants' assistant head coach and special teams coordinator in 2026. A former UCLA safety and 2008 Washington seventh-round pick, he was Baltimore Ravens special teams coordinator from 2019 to 2025 after joining John Harbaugh's staff in 2014.

hc.name: Nick Sirianni
hc.bio: Nick Sirianni is the Philadelphia Eagles' head coach in 2026, hired January 24, 2021 and given a multiyear extension May 19, 2025. He played wide receiver at Mount Union (1999–2003) and was Colts offensive coordinator (2018–2020) before Philadelphia; through 2025 he is 59–26 in the regular season with a Super Bowl LIX win after the 2024 season. The 2025 Eagles went 11–6 and lost a wild-card game to San Francisco.

oc.name: Sean Mannion
oc.bio: Sean Mannion is the Philadelphia Eagles' offensive coordinator in 2026, hired January 29, 2026. An Oregon State quarterback drafted by the St. Louis Rams in the third round in 2015, he played for the Rams, Vikings, and Seahawks, then was a Packers offensive assistant in 2024 and Packers quarterbacks coach in 2025.

dc.name: Vic Fangio
dc.bio: Vic Fangio is the Philadelphia Eagles' defensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2024. A 40-plus-year coach, he was Denver Broncos head coach (2019–2021) and has coordinated defenses for Carolina, Indianapolis, Houston, San Francisco, Chicago, Miami, and Philadelphia (also a 2022 Eagles consultant).

st.name: Michael Clay
st.bio: Michael Clay is the Philadelphia Eagles' special teams coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2021. He played linebacker at Oregon and was an Eagles and 49ers special teams assistant (2014–2020) before Nick Sirianni named him coordinator.

hc.name: Mike Macdonald
hc.bio: Mike Macdonald is the Seattle Seahawks' head coach in 2026, hired January 31, 2024. He attended the University of Georgia, graduated summa cum laude in finance in 2010, and coached high school football at Cedar Shoals while a student before joining Georgia's staff as a graduate assistant. He was Michigan defensive coordinator in 2021 and Ravens DC in 2022–2023; Seattle went 10–7 in 2024 and 14–3 in 2025, winning Super Bowl LX over New England (Wikipedia: 24–10 regular season, 3–0 postseason).

oc.name: Brian Fleury
oc.bio: Brian Fleury is the Seattle Seahawks' offensive coordinator in 2026, hired after Klint Kubiak left to become Raiders head coach. He played quarterback at Maryland and Towson and was 49ers tight ends coach (2022–2024) and run-game coordinator/tight ends coach in 2025, after earlier NFL quality-control and linebacker jobs with Buffalo, Cleveland, and San Francisco.

dc.name: Aden Durde
dc.bio: Aden Durde is the Seattle Seahawks' defensive coordinator in 2026, retained since 2024. A British former linebacker who played for Carolina, Kansas City, and NFL Europe, he was Cowboys defensive line coach (2021–2023) after Falcons quality-control and outside-linebacker roles.

st.name: Jay Harbaugh
st.bio: Jay Harbaugh is the Seattle Seahawks' special teams coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2024. Wikipedia identifies him as Jim Harbaugh's son and John Harbaugh's nephew; staff records list him as Ravens offensive quality-control coach from 2012 to 2014 before the Seattle ST job.

hc.name: Kyle Shanahan
hc.bio: Kyle Shanahan is the San Francisco 49ers' head coach in 2026, hired February 6, 2017. He played wide receiver at Texas after a Duke redshirt year and was Falcons offensive coordinator in Super Bowl LI; through 2025 he is 82–67 in the regular season with Super Bowl losses in LIV and LVIII. The 2025 49ers went 12–5, beat Philadelphia in the wild-card round, and lost 41–6 to Seattle in the divisional round.

oc.name: Klay Kubiak
oc.bio: Klay Kubiak is the San Francisco 49ers' offensive coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2025. He played quarterback at Colorado State (2007–2010), is the son of former NFL coach Gary Kubiak, and rose through the 49ers staff from defensive quality control (2021) to assistant quarterbacks, passing-game specialist (2024), then OC.

dc.name: Raheem Morris
dc.bio: Raheem Morris is the San Francisco 49ers' defensive coordinator in 2026. He was Atlanta Falcons head coach in 2024–2025 (fired January 4, 2026) and Tampa Bay head coach from 2009 to 2011, plus Rams defensive coordinator (2021–2023) and Super Bowl LVI staff member.

st.name: Brant Boyer
st.bio: Brant Boyer is the San Francisco 49ers' special teams coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2025. A former linebacker drafted by Miami and later with Jacksonville and Cleveland, he was Jets special teams coordinator from 2016 to 2024.

hc.name: Todd Bowles
hc.bio: Todd Bowles is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' head coach in 2026, elevated March 30, 2022 after serving as Buccaneers defensive coordinator (2019–2021) and winning Super Bowl LV. He played safety at Temple and for Washington (Super Bowl XXII) and was Jets head coach from 2015 to 2018. Through 2025 his Tampa regular-season record is 35–33, with NFC South titles in 2022–2024; the 2025 Buccaneers finished 8–9.

oc.name: Zac Robinson
oc.bio: Zac Robinson is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' offensive coordinator in 2026. An Oklahoma State quarterback drafted by New England in the seventh round in 2010, he was Rams assistant (2019–2023) and Atlanta Falcons offensive coordinator in 2024–2025.

dc.name: Todd Bowles
dc.bio: Todd Bowles is listed as the Buccaneers' 2026 defensive coordinator equivalent: the official coaches roster and 2026 season staff list name no separate defensive coordinator, and Bowles remains head coach after serving as Tampa Bay DC from 2019 to 2021. He previously was Arizona Cardinals defensive coordinator (2013–2014) and won AP Assistant Coach of the Year in 2014.

st.name: Danny Smith
st.bio: Danny Smith is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' special teams coordinator in 2026. Wikipedia lists him as Daniel Thomas Smith (born November 7, 1953); staff history shows Eagles ST/DB (1995–1998), Lions tight ends (1999–2000), Bills ST (2001–2003), Washington ST (2004–2012), and Steelers ST coordinator (2013–2025).

hc.name: Dan Quinn
hc.bio: Dan Quinn is the Washington Commanders' head coach in 2026, hired February 3, 2024. He played defensive line at Salisbury (1989–1993), was Seahawks DC for Super Bowl XLVIII, Falcons head coach (2015–2020, Super Bowl LI), and Cowboys DC (2021–2023). Washington went 12–5 and reached the NFC Championship in 2024, then 5–12 in 2025.

oc.name: David Blough
oc.bio: David Blough is the Washington Commanders' offensive coordinator in 2026, promoted January 10, 2026. A former Purdue quarterback who played for Cleveland, Detroit, Minnesota, and Arizona, he was Commanders assistant quarterbacks coach in 2024–2025 and interim quarterbacks coach for the final four games of 2025.

dc.name: Daronte Jones
dc.bio: Daronte Jones is the Washington Commanders' defensive coordinator in 2026, hired January 30, 2026. Wikipedia notes prior defensive coordinator jobs at Bowie State and LSU; NFL staff history lists Dolphins assistant DBs (2016–2017), Bengals cornerbacks (2018–2019), and Vikings defensive backs/pass-game coordinator (2020, 2022–2025).

st.name: Larry Izzo
st.bio: Larry Izzo is the Washington Commanders' special teams coordinator in 2026, a role he has held since 2024. A former Rice linebacker and three-time Pro Bowl special teamer with New England, he won three Super Bowls as a player and was Seahawks ST coordinator from 2021 to 2023 after Giants, Texans, and Seahawks assistant ST jobs.
